notice: Independent research review only; never an eo-lifecycle-review/v1 certification.
rationale: Independent reading: held EO 9301 (8 FR 1825, Feb. 9, 1943) sets a 48-hour minimum wartime workweek 'for the duration of the war' (para. 1) with WMC administration; held EO 9607 (10 FR 11191, Aug. 30, 1945): 'Executive Order 9301 of February 9, 1943, establishing a minimum wartime workweek of forty-eight hours, be, and it is hereby, revoked', no condition or savings. Whole revocation; independent status NO, agrees. Refutation: the 'duration of the war' own term could not have ended before Aug. 30, 1945 on any held record, so no earlier end displaces the cited one (and an earlier end would leave the NO unchanged). D6: catalog 'See: EO 9333' is a cross-reference lead, not an acting event; EO 9332 (Apr. 1943) merely refers to WMC directives under EO 9301 and amends nothing; no later held instrument revives or re-enacts the workweek rule. Nothing ignored. Accept.
